04 /16.02.2024  Heard the learned counsels for the parties.
The petitioner is an accused in a case registered under sections 363/366-A/376-E/34 of the Indian Penal Code and sections 5 & 6 POCSO Act.

The learned senior counsel for the petitioner has submitted that this is not a case of rape rather he says that it may pertain to section 9 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act and in such situation it would be considered a minor offence as compared to the allegation of rape.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has also stated that both parties are closely related to each other.

It is further submitted that as per the records available, after conducting marriage they have lived together for around 7 to 8 months and no alarm or adverse report was made by the wife or the alleged victim.

Counsel has particularly relied on the evidence of Sunita Devi and Deepa Devi who are immediate Aunties and closely related to the informant herself and pointed out that the girl in question had come for a birthday party on the occasion of birthday of her cousin and on that occasion petitioner had also come there and both of them had run away and thereafter conducted marriage and they lived together for seven months and this has been supported by the evidence of the aforesaid relatives and he has pointed out that it is only when at a later stage on the 'Shradh' ceremony of another person the mother of the victim had come and then she had returned with her mother and finally the case was lodged.

Counsel, therefore, says in between there was no complaint whatsoever Mritunjay Paswan @ Suraj Paswan @ ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130247432/
1 and they were living together as husband and wife and therefore it may not be considered as a case of rape.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that when the marriage has been solemnized then there can be no question of rape.

It is further pointed out that in the Exception 2 under section 375 IPC also offence of rape cannot be made out because as per the impugned order on the date of occurrence she was over fifteen years and, therefore it may not be an offence of rape.
It is submitted that based on the aforesaid circumstances, the petitioner may be allowed the privilege of bail.

Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the bail petition and submitted that the allegations are serious in nature and cognizance has been taken under sections 366 & 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code, section 6 of the POCSO Act and section 9 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act.

The learned counsel further says that from the allegations itself made in the complaint which was converted into FIR, it is clear that there was possible abduction or kidnapping, also possible marriage and then consummation of marriage thereafter, therefore, in such circumstances,
the petitioner may not be allowed the privilege of bail.
Having heard both counsels, gone through the records of the case and in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am not inclined to release the petitioner, named above, on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application of the petitioner, above named, is rejected.

(Ratnaker Bhengra, J.) Sharda/
